claims.text: USGS recorded a magnitude 7.7 earthquake on 14 August 2026 at 21:58:21 UTC, located 68 km NNW of Ende, Indonesia, at a depth of 10 km, resulting from reverse faulting where the Australia and Sunda plates converge. USGS's own monitoring detected no tsunami, assessed a Yellow PAGER alert level, and estimated approximately 2 million people exposed to strong-to-violent shaking (maximum MMI 8.38); 42 felt reports had been received as of retrieval.

GDACS's earthquake report (event id 1558059, episode 1725109) rates the event a Red alert for high humanitarian impact, with about 1.2 million people within zones of MMI VII or greater shaking, magnitude 7.7 at a depth of 10 km, and a recorded tsunami with a maximum wave height of 1.7 m. GDACS reports at least 51 deaths and approximately 5,000 people displaced, noting rescue teams are working to clear streets blocked by landslides and reach survivors trapped under rubble.

Re-checked 17 August 2026: GDACS's event report (event id 1558059, episode 1725109, Red alert, score 2.4) now carries media citations (Punch NG: "The 7.7-magnitude quake early on Saturday killed 54 people and injured more than 100" and "Earthquake kills 54, displaces 12,800 in Indonesia"; Asahi: "a powerful earthquake killed at least 54 people, injured dozens and damaged hundreds of homes") putting the toll at 54 deaths, more than 100 injured and about 12,800 people displaced -- up from the 51 deaths/~5,000 displaced recorded on 16 August. These figures are attributed to media sources referenced on the GDACS page rather than to a dedicated GDACS/Sendai casualty assessment. The recorded tsunami remains at a maximum wave height of about 1.68 m.

USGS's earthquake catalog for the area around Flores/Ende, Indonesia (14-18 August 2026, M5.5+) lists a sustained aftershock sequence following the M7.7 mainshock (14 August 21:58:21 UTC): a M6.1 aftershock 58 km N of Ende (14 August 22:28:37 UTC), M5.9 36 km NE of Labuan Bajo (22:13:50 UTC), M5.6 61 km NNW of Ende (22:18:06 UTC), M5.5 61 km ENE of Ruteng (22:17:00 UTC) and M5.5 49 km NE of Labuan Bajo (22:37:17 UTC) on 14 August, a further M5.5 76 km N of Ruteng on 16 August (06:51:47 UTC), and continuing seismicity through at least 17 August with a M5.7 event 65 km NNW of Ende at 00:46:45 UTC.

Re-checked 18 August 2026: GDACS's event report (event id 1558059, episode 1725109, still Red alert, score now 2.1, down from 2.4 on 17 August) shows population exposure to MMI VII+ shaking revised to about 870,000 (down from ~1.2 million cited 16-17 August); the recorded tsunami remains at a maximum wave height of about 1.68 m. The page's media citations now show only one casualty figure, from catnat.net (French-language): "Un puissant seisme de magnitude 7,7 a secoue samedi matin l'est de l'Indonesie... Il a fait au moins 68 morts" ("a powerful magnitude-7.7 earthquake shook eastern Indonesia... it caused at least 68 deaths") -- up from the 54 deaths cited via Punch NG/Asahi on 17 August. No displaced or injured figure is cited on the page today. As with the prior update, this is a media citation referenced on the GDACS page rather than a dedicated GDACS/Sendai casualty assessment, but per this record's established practice of adopting the GDACS page's most recent cited media toll, the headline death toll is updated to 68. USGS's PAGER product for event us6000tkt2 remains a Yellow alert, last updated 15 August 2026, with no change to its own casualty modeling.

Indonesian Humanitarian Coordination Platform Situation Report No. 3 (MPBI, 19 August 2026), citing provisional BNPB data as of 19 August 2026, 09:00 WIB: 71 deaths, 1,182 injured, 40,145 displaced, and 11,950 houses damaged (5,518 severely, 1,924 moderately, 4,508 slightly), with 217 education facilities, 96 health facilities, 46 government offices and 77 places of worship damaged; aftershocks continue frequently, raising landslide risk in already susceptible locations.

description: A magnitude 7.7 shallow earthquake struck off Flores Island in East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia, on 14 August 2026 at 21:58:21 UTC, centered about 68 km NNW of Ende at a depth of 10 km, where the Australia and Sunda plates converge; GDACS recorded a tsunami with a maximum wave height of about 1.68 m. Indonesia's BNPB, via the Indonesian Humanitarian Coordination Platform's Situation Report No. 3 (19 August), puts the toll at 71 deaths, 1,182 injured and 40,145 displaced, with 11,950 houses damaged; rescue teams have been working to clear landslide-blocked streets and reach survivors trapped under rubble. A sustained aftershock sequence has followed, the largest a M6.1 event 58 km north of Ende, with continuing seismicity raising landslide risk in already susceptible locations. USGS assessed a Yellow PAGER alert with roughly 2 million people exposed to strong-to-violent shaking, while GDACS's Red-alert report estimates about 870,000 people within zones of MMI VII or greater.

impact.summary: BNPB's provisional data as of 19 August 2026, per the Indonesian Humanitarian Coordination Platform's Situation Report No. 3, puts the toll at 71 deaths, 1,182 injured and 40,145 displaced, with 11,950 houses damaged (5,518 severely). GDACS's Red-alert report has not yet incorporated this update and estimates about 870,000 people exposed to MMI VII or greater shaking. A tsunami with a maximum wave height of about 1.68 m was recorded, and aftershocks up to M6.1 have continued; USGS's PAGER alert remains Yellow.

name: M7.7 Earthquake, Flores, Indonesia

updates.text: BNPB's provisional data, per the Indonesian Humanitarian Coordination Platform's Situation Report No. 3, raised the toll to 71 deaths, 1,182 injured and 40,145 displaced (up from 68 deaths and 12,800 displaced), with 11,950 houses damaged across the affected area.

Media tolls cited on GDACS's event report rose to at least 68 deaths (via catnat.net), up from 54 the previous day; GDACS revised its estimate of people exposed to MMI VII or greater shaking down to about 870,000 from about 1.2 million, and its alert score to 2.1 from 2.4. The recorded tsunami remains at a maximum wave height of about 1.68 m.

Media reports cited on GDACS's event report (Punch NG, Asahi) put the toll at 54 deaths, more than 100 injured and about 12,800 people displaced — up from 51 deaths and approximately 5,000 displaced a day earlier — with hundreds of homes damaged.

GDACS rated the event a Red alert for high humanitarian impact, reporting at least 51 deaths and approximately 5,000 people displaced, with about 1.2 million people within zones of MMI VII or greater shaking and a recorded tsunami of up to 1.7 m; rescue teams worked to clear landslide-blocked streets and reach survivors trapped under rubble.
